findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
The bathroom that is off to the side of the bar is observed to have coving that is pulled away from the wall. There were observed to be multiple fast-moving roaches that came out of this coving when the coving was disturbed. 

In the main men’s bathroom, there were observed to be two dead baby roaches, one on the floor and one in the cabinets. 

In the kitchen, there was observed to be a fast-moving roach under the soda fountain area and another fast-moving roach in the back corner that went into coving that is pulled away from the wall. There were over a dozen dead roaches of all life stages on the floor throughout the kitchen. 

Throughout the kitchen, there is observed to be missing coving and coving that is no longer sealed to the wall. There is also observed to be cardboard that is being kept in the kitchen. There needs to be attention to cleaning as well to ensure that the dead roaches are being regularly cleaned up. The back door was observed to be cracked open, potentially allowing more pests to enter the facility. 

The PIC was unsure of where pest control records would be kept. In the past, Terminix and Bacon’s were listed as the pest control companies. The PIC stated that pest control has come frequently in the past two months. 

A follow up is scheduled for 8/3/2026 to ensure that cleaning is occurring throughout the facility to clean dead roaches, that pest control is regularly coming, and that proper actions are being taken by the facility to reduce pest presence (removing cardboard, keeping the back door shut, sealing coving, etc.).
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment:

findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several areas in need of cleaning or repair in the facility. 
-The first area is the wall behind the soda syrups. The wall has a large opening. Ensure that this opening is sealed to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface. It is okay to have the hoses run through the wall, but the wall must be closed around the hoses.
-The second area is on the right side of the bar. There is a large hole that opens to an air conditioner unit. This hole must be closed either by adding a door to service the air conditioner, or sealing off the wall.
-The third area is the back room in the kitchen with standing coolers and a chest freezer. Inspector observed this area to be soiled along the edges of the walls. Ensure these areas are cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean.
-Facility could also benefit from a general cleaning since pest presence has been observed for a while now. 

Ensure all of these violations are corrected by the next routine inspection in 2026.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector noted several live cockroaches on glue traps around the facility. All glue traps were observed to have some amount of cockroaches on them. PIC informed inspector that pest control comes once a week on Mondays. This indicates that pest control alone is not enough to keep the cockroach population down. Inspector recommends a deep cleaning of all dark and unused areas, as well as behind and inside equipment. Cockroaches can hide in these places and maintain a pest presence in the kitchen even when pest control is active. Ensure the cockroaches are eradicated to maintain clean and sanitary food-contact surfaces.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the CFPM to not have an allergen certification. Talked with the CFPM about allergen certifications and provided the class handout. Ensure that all CFPMs on staff receive allergen training.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.
